title: bug: JetBrains protected PATH filter keeps entries as written, so an edge-quoted or space-padded entry escapes the project check
description:
MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedPathEntries validates unquoted(entry) (trim plus surrounding ") but keeps the as-written entry.
- Windows: libuv's PATH search strips one leading or trailing ' or ". Verified on node v24.16.0: PATH=C:\Windows\System32' still runs whoami. So `<project>'` passes isOutsideProject (realpath ENOENT, and the normalized form differs from the project), and the daemon's bare-name spawns then search the project.
- POSIX: ` /x` survives as a relative execvp entry.
VS Code fixed this in RF06b reopen 1 (task-032c973941bc41d9b051eedacb7de0b6): keep the validated spelling and drop entries ending in a quote.
definitionOfDone: JetBrains protectedPathEntries/protectedDaemonEnvironment keep only validated spellings (trimmed, surrounding quotes removed) and drop any entry that still starts or ends with ' or ". A test shows `<project>'` dropped and a space-padded outside entry kept unpadded.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX (GREEN) in MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:575-584. Change nothing else in the file.
(1) `protectedPathEntries`: map each `split(File.pathSeparator)` entry through `unquoted` FIRST, then filter, so the list it returns holds the validated spellings. Drop an entry whose validated spelling still starts or ends with ' or ", then require `RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject(entry, basePath)`. Suggested shape: `path.split(File.pathSeparator).map { unquoted(it) }.filter { entry -> "'\"".none { entry.startsWith(it) || entry.endsWith(it) } && RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject(entry, basePath) }`.
(2) `nodeOnProtectedPath`: the entries are already unquoted, so use `.map { File(it, if (windows) "node.exe" else "node") }` and remove the second `unquoted(...)`.
(3) `unquoted` keeps exactly `entry.trim().removeSurrounding("\"")`. That matches VS Code's `entry.trim().replace(/^"(.*)"$/, '$1')`. Do not add a second trim or single-quote stripping: a dropped entry is the fail-closed answer.
(4) Update the one-line comment above protectedPathEntries to give the why. libuv's Windows PATH search strips one leading or trailing ' or ", so `<project>'` searches the project. execvp reads a space-padded entry as relative. So each kept entry is exactly the spelling that was validated. Keep the file's terse comment density.
Error handling: add no new IO or throwing call. isOutsideProject already catches Exception and IOError and returns false, so a malformed entry (NUL, an illegal Windows char such as `"`, a trailing space) is dropped, never kept. nodeOnProtectedPath keeps its `isFile` probe, which returns false on any error.
protectedDaemonEnvironment, the spawn and stop builders, and ManagedVmPanel.kt:122/137 inherit the fix with no edit. The LEGACY profile never calls these functions, so it is unchanged.
Re-run the focused class command from step 1 (under the lease): RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest must be all green.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN. protectedPathEntries now maps through unquoted FIRST, then drops any entry whose validated spelling starts/ends with ' or ", then requires isOutsideProject(entry). nodeOnProtectedPath no longer unquotes a second time. unquoted unchanged. Comment above protectedPathEntries gives the libuv/execvp why. No new IO. Focused RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest (jetbrains-gradle lease held): BUILD SUCCESSFUL, :test executed (not UP-TO-DATE).

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW of this task's diff only (load adversarial-self-review). Check each item and record the answer in the step note:
(1) Every PATH string that reaches a child process or File lookup under PROTECTED is exactly the string isOutsideProject validated. That covers protectedPathEntries, nodeOnProtectedPath, protectedDaemonEnvironment and ManagedVmPanel, with no as-written spelling left.
(2) Windows: `<project>'`, `'<project>'`, `"<project>"'` and `<project>"` are dropped. A legit quoted entry such as `"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd"` is kept unquoted and still works, because libuv and cmd accept spaces in an unquoted entry.
(3) POSIX: ` /x` is kept as `/x`, and `"/x"` is kept as `/x`, no longer a relative `"/x"` resolved under a daemon child's cwd.
(4) Padding inside the quotes (`" /x"`) leaves ` /x`, which isOutsideProject rejects (relative on POSIX, InvalidPathException on Windows), so it is dropped and never kept padded.
(5) A quoted entry containing the separator is split by File.pathSeparator into edge-quoted halves, so both halves are dropped (fail closed).
(6) No new IO, LEGACY untouched, and `git diff --stat` touches exactly the two planned files.
Windows trailing-dot spellings are OUT OF SCOPE: JetBrains already refuses them through toRealPath/GetFullPathName (mem:gotcha-windows-node-namespaced-realpath). Do not change them. Fix anything the review finds within these two files and re-run step 3's command if code changed.

Edge cases: lone `"` (removeSurrounding no-op, starts with quote) and `""` (-> empty, not absolute) are dropped; `"C:\x "` trailing space -> InvalidPathException -> dropped. (6) Pure function, no new IO, no shared state, LEGACY never calls these; `git diff --stat -- moe-jetbrains` = exactly the 2 planned files, +13/-5. executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under the PROTECTED profile, the JetBrains PATH filter (MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedPathEntries, used by protectedDaemonEnvironment, nodeOnProtectedPath and ManagedVmPanel) returns each kept entry in the exact spelling it validated: trimmed, with one surrounding pair of double quotes removed. It drops every entry whose validated spelling still starts or ends with ' or ". So `<project>'` (which libuv on Windows reads as `<project>`) never reaches the daemon PATH. A space-padded or double-quoted outside entry is kept unpadded and unquoted, so execvp never sees it as a relative entry.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Mirror VS Code exactly: drop only a trailing quote. Rejected because the DoD says starts OR ends. A leading quote already fails isAbsolute on every OS, so the extra check is defense in depth and costs nothing. (2) Strip single quotes as well, the way libuv does, and keep the result. Rejected: a rewrite widens what is accepted, while dropping fails closed and only an unusual PATH loses an entry. (3) Dedupe kept entries, as VS Code's protectedDaemonEnvironment does. Rejected as scope creep: duplicates are harmless.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: protectedPathEntries is the single choke point. protectedDaemonEnvironment (spawn and stopBuilder) and ManagedVmPanel both go through it, so a two-function edit fixes all of them. Both functions run only under PROTECTED, so LEGACY cannot regress. Kotlin tests cannot run in WSL (no JDK): use cmd.exe with gradlew.bat under the `jetbrains-gradle` lease, plus --rerun and the counts check from the test-results XML.
risks: Do not keep the second `unquoted` in nodeOnProtectedPath. Double-unquoting is harmless today, but it hides which spelling was validated.
The test must keep the exact whole-map assertEquals. Without it, an implementation that still returns `it` passes an all-outside check.
On Windows, `<outside>"` is already dropped by InvalidPathException, so the `<project>'` and padded cases carry the Windows RED. On Linux all four new cases go RED.
A 5s BUILD SUCCESSFUL with `:test UP-TO-DATE` ran zero tests. Always use --rerun and confirm the XML counts.
Trailing-dot Windows spellings are out of scope. JetBrains already refuses them through toRealPath (mem:gotcha-windows-node-namespaced-realpath).
